\section[bonam noctem]{bonam noctem — real grammar, not a real citation}

\label{lesson:LA-C30-bonam-noctem}



\begin{quote}
\textbf{Warm-up.} {[}PAUSE 2s{]} You already have \emph{bonus} (good) and \emph{nox} (night, last lesson). Put them together for "good night" — but the case they end up in is the real lesson here.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: bonam noctem — why accusative, not nominative}]
\textbf{Bonam noctem} = "\textbf{good night}" — but notice: \textbf{not} \emph{bona nox} (nominative). Latin wishes and exclamations conventionally use the \textbf{accusative} case — the same "\textbf{Accusative of Exclamation}" behind the genuinely attested \emph{Fēlīcem nātālem!} ("happy birthday!," short for \emph{tibi fēlīcem diem nātālem exoptō}, "I wish you a happy birthday"). Grammatically, \emph{bonam noctem} is a compressed exclamation — something like "{[}\textbf{I wish you}{]} a good night," with the verb left unstated, the same kind of ellipsis you'd find in a letter opening like "\emph{Cicero Atticō salūtem} {[}\emph{dīcit}{]}" ("Cicero sends greetings to Atticus"). The bare nominative \emph{bona nox} would work too (with an implied "\emph{sit}," "may it be"), but the accusative is the more natural, idiomatic choice for a wish like this.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: Be honest: real grammar, not a real citation}]
Here's the careful part, matching the same honesty already applied to \emph{quōmodo tē habēs?}, \emph{nihil est}, and \emph{crās tē vidēbō} earlier in this arc: the \textbf{accusative-of-wishing} principle itself is genuine, solid Classical Latin grammar. But this \textbf{specific fixed phrase}, \emph{bonam noctem}, is \textbf{not} actually attested as a Roman farewell formula in any surviving classical text — it appears to be a later, post-classical convention, built correctly from real grammar but not itself a citation. Treat the grammar as reliable and the exact phrase as a well-formed construction, not a quotation from a Roman text.
\end{grammarlens}
